title: Bounded separation of root modules implies weak stability of a fraction field
statement: Let $A$ be an integral domain with a real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value $G$, and let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ be its fraction field [def-weil-field], with $|a/b|=G(a)/G(b)$, assumed nontrivial. Suppose $\operatorname{char}(K)=p>0$. In an algebraic closure $\overline K$, put $K^{1/p}=\{z:z^p\in K\}$ and $A^{1/p}=\{z:z^p\in A\}$, endowed with $N(z)=|z^p|^{1/p}$. Suppose that for every finitely generated $A$-submodule $M\subseteq A^{1/p}$ (that is, $M=\sum_{j=1}^r Am_j$ for finitely many $m_j$) and every nonzero $x\in M$, there is an $A$-linear map $\lambda:M\to A$ with $\lambda(x)\ne0$ and a real $B>0$ such that $G(\lambda(y))\le B N(y)$ for all $y\in M$. Then for every finite extension $L/K$, every $K$-basis $v_1,\ldots,v_d$ of $L$, and its minimal-polynomial spectral norm $s_{L/K}$ [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm], there are real $c,C>0$ such that $$c\max_i|a_i|\le s_{L/K}(\sum_i a_iv_i)\le C\max_i|a_i|\qquad(a_i\in K).$$ Neither completeness of $K$ nor separability of $L/K$ is assumed.

proof.text: Put $K_1=K^{1/p}$ and $A_1=A^{1/p}$. The characteristic-$p$ identities $(z+w)^p=z^p+w^p$ and $(az)^p=a^pz^p$ show directly that $K_1$ is a field, $A_1$ an $A$-submodule, and $N$ a definite multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value extending $|\cdot|$ on $K$. Fix any finite-dimensional $V\subseteq K_1$ with basis $v_1,\ldots,v_r$. If $r=0$, take both coordinate constants to be $1$. Otherwise write $v_i^p=b_i/a_i$ with $a_i,b_i\in A$, $a_i\ne0$, and put $m_i=a_iv_i$. Then $m_i^p=a_i^{p-1}b_i\in A$, so $M=\sum_i Am_i\subseteq A_1$ is finitely generated and has $K$-span $V$. For $y=\sum_i q_im_i$, writing $q_i=c_i/d_i$ in $K$ and taking $d=\prod_i d_i\ne0$ gives $dy\in M$.

proof.text: Given an $A$-linear $\lambda:M\to A$ with $G(\lambda(x))\le B N(x)$ on $M$, define $h(y)=\lambda(dy)/d\in K$ for any nonzero $d\in A$ with $dy\in M$. This is independent of $d$: if also $ey\in M$, then $e\lambda(dy)=\lambda(edy)=d\lambda(ey)$. For $y,z\in V$ choose one denominator putting both in $M$; additivity of $\lambda$ gives $h(y+z)=h(y)+h(z)$. For $q=b/a\in K$, choose $dy\in M$; then $ad(qy)=bdy\in M$, giving $h(qy)=\lambda(bdy)/(ad)=q h(y)$. Thus $h$ is $K$-linear. Moreover $$|h(y)|=G(\lambda(dy))/G(d)\le B N(dy)/G(d)=B N(y).$$ This uses $N(dy)=G(d)N(y)$, so no norm estimate is lost by denominators.

e0$. Choose $r$ such forms $h_1,\ldots,h_r$ with zero common kernel: start with $V$, and, whenever the current intersection $W$ of kernels is nonzero, choose $0
e y\in W$ and a separating form nonzero at $y$. Its restriction to $W$ is a nonzero map to the one-dimensional space $K$, so intersecting with its kernel lowers the dimension by exactly one. After $r$ choices the dimension is zero. Retain a bound $B_j>0$ for each $h_j$.

proof.text: The square matrix $H=(h_j(v_i))_{j,i}$ has zero kernel and is invertible over $K$. Write $T=H^{-1}$, $D=\max_{i,j}|T_{ij}|>0$, and $B_*=\max_j B_j>0$. For $y=\sum_i q_iv_i$ the equality $(q_i)_i=T(h_j(y))_j$ and the ultrametric inequality give $$\max_i|q_i|\le D\max_j|h_j(y)|\le D B_* N(y).$$ Conversely $$N(y)\le\max_i |q_i|N(v_i)\le C_V\max_i|q_i|,$$ where $C_V=\max_iN(v_i)>0$. Taking $c_V=(DB_*)^{-1}>0$ proves both coordinate bounds for this arbitrary $V$ and its original basis. No topological finite-dimensional theorem over an incomplete base has been invoked.

proof.text: Every finite-dimensional subspace of $K_1$ now satisfies the hypothesis of [lem-trf-frobenius-root-coordinate-test], with the same field $K$, positive characteristic $p$, and the root norm $N(z)=|z^p|^{1/p}$. That theorem gives exactly the two displayed bounds for every finite $L/K$ and every basis of $L$, with its minimal-polynomial spectral norm. Its hypotheses impose neither completeness nor separability, so it applies to the extensions in the statement.
